newsitem.title: USA: Leaders end summit day, Yeltsin tired.
newsitem.headline: Leaders end summit day, Yeltsin tired.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, tired after two days of talks at a Group of Seven summit, left an official dinner early and missed a gala concert on Saturday night.
"He was tired, he was just tired," White House aide Daniel Tarullo told reporters.

Yeltsin went back to his hotel after leaving the dinner of rattlesnake and buffalo about 20 minutes early. But a Kremlin official said he would take part in Sunday's closing events of the three-day summit.

"He is in his residence, he had decided that he would prefer not to take part in this event," a Kremlin official said after Yeltsin skipped the concert. "Tomorrow's meetings will go ahead according to plan."
The dinner was at a restaurant in nearby Morrison that specializes in foods from the 19th century fur trade.

Yeltsin had been scheduled to leave the dinner with leaders of the G7 countries -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- and attend a "Saturday Night at the Summit" concert featuring singers Michael Bolton, Lyle Lovett and Eartha Kitt.
At the start of the summit on Friday, Yeltsin had looked fit and fully recovered from two heart attacks last year. But on Saturday he looked tired and moved stiffly.
However, during a meeting with American businessman, he impressed them with his zeal for bilateral projects and his commitment to attracting U.S. companies.
On Sunday, the G7 leaders and Yeltsin hold a final session before wrapping up the summit with a series of news conferences.

In their communique, they are set to present a united front urging China to ensure Hong Kong's civil liberties and guarantee free elections after Beijing takes control of the British colony on July 1.
They also planned to express their determination to revive the stalled Middle East peace process.
"Restoring the sense of security and confidence among Israelis and Palestinians is essential," a draft of the communique said.

Yeltsin arrived at the Saturday night dinner wearing a suit and tie. But on seeing Clinton, who was wearing brown cowboy boots and a bolero tie, he removed his tie and unbuttoned the top button of his white shirt.

The menu was medallions of buffalo and something called "fried squash blossoms filled with wild mushrooms and rattlesnake." It may have been the strangest summit meal since Yeltsin served Clinton moose lips.

There was laughter over who would answer Clinton's appeal to join him in wearing cowboy boots. German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was horrified at the prospect but Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto pulled them on as did Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien and British Prime Minister Tony Blair.
Before leaving this Rocky Mountain city, the leaders planned to release a statement urging Bosnia's former warring factions to step up the pace of the peace process.

The summit partners on Saturday papered over differences on plans to pull American peacekeepers out of Bosnia by mid-1998 and concentrated on telling the former warring parties that aid could be stopped if they let the peace process falter.
They singled out Croatia and Serbia for special criticism, faulting them for lack of commitment to the peace process.
